newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia lets monopolies negotiate own tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Russia lets monopolies negotiate own tariffs.

text.p: Russia will let its natural gas, electricity and railway monopolies negotiate lower tariffs with industrial consumers in an effort to improve cash flows at the giant tax payers, a senior official said on Thursday.

Deputy Economy Minister Vyacheslav Morgunov said the government had approved a ministry plan to partially free up the heavily-regulated sectors to allow lower prices over the second half of the year to customers who paid in cash.
"The goal is to increase the ability of producers to give discounts in order to attract payment in cash," he told a news conference.

A non-payments crisis in which industry and consumers owe each other, leaving the budget paralysed by low tax revenues, is slowing Russia's overall economic growth. Cleaning up the mess is one of the government's top priorities.

Gazprom is the gas monopoly and Unified Energy System, or UES, the electricity monopoly. The two companies are among Russia's largest tax payers but they are also owed more than all other companies combined.
Morgunov said only 10 percent of gas was paid for in cash. The rate for electricity was 12-15 percent, while for railways it was 40 percent.

Allowing the monopolies to provide discounts to cash-paying customers would double gas cash payments by the end of the year. Cash payments to the electricity and railway monopolies should rise 50 percent, Morgunov said.
But there are questions over the plan.
"There is a certain risk because of this freedom," Morgunov said. "What I have said is a signal to the natural monopolies that there must be an effect from the discounts."
The government will also increase passenger railway subsidies to help offset freight costs. Morgunov said no level had been set but that average rail freight costs could fall by up to four percent.
